requirements.evidence: app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:16 matches the contract signature; :18-26 runs in a transaction, locks the queue row and reads fresh is_active; :28 and :62-85 implement the 3-call fairness rule; :87-110 locks each candidate and re-checks waiting; :119-141 applies priority DESC, issued_at ASC, id ASC per mode; :48-50 throws NoWaitingTicketsException; docs/business-rules.md:121 and docs/architecture.md:122 document it.

conventions.evidence: Domain write lives in app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php as required; tests ship in tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php; docs and CHANGELOG are updated (docs/business-rules.md:121, docs/architecture.md:122, CHANGELOG.md:21); no Livewire/authorization added per task scope. One deviation: the new public __invoke has no PHPDoc (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:16), despite the 'PHPDoc on public methods you touched' convention.

security.evidence: app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:18-26 reads queue state under lockForUpdate instead of trusting the stale passed model; :90-103 locks and re-validates the candidate; :105-110 assigns only the three allowed fields directly rather than via mass assignment; no user-controlled input, raw SQL, or unescaped output; authorization is explicitly out of scope in task.md:11-12 and task.md:64-67.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php covers ordering and id tie-break (:43-76), queue isolation (:78-90), all three modes (:129-158), fairness trigger/reset/history (:160-248), inactive stale queue (:250-263), all NoWaitingTicketsException paths (:265-294) and returned/write-once state (:296-315). Gaps: the 'concurrently called' test (:109) calls Ticket::call before the action, so the snapshot already filters it and the locked re-check branch at app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:101 is never exercised; the fairness fallback at app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:32-46 is untested; :225's title mentions normal_only but only priority_only calls are made.

simplicity.evidence: Single invokable action with no new service/repository layer, reusing the Queue/Ticket models and TicketStatus enum. Minor duplication: the waiting-normal existence query appears twice (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:37-41 and :80-84), and :110 refresh() issues an extra query although the saved model already reflects the call.

readability.evidence: Clear names (fairnessApplies, takeNext, candidateIds, restrictToNormal), small focused methods, and comments explaining the concurrency re-check (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:32-35, :99-100). Tests use descriptive Pest names and arrange data readably.

scope.evidence: The diff touches only the action, the CallMode enum, the exception, its test file, the two docs required by the task (docs/business-rules.md:121, docs/architecture.md:122) and the CHANGELOG entry (CHANGELOG.md:21); no unrelated refactors or features.

issues.explanation: The fairness fallback that re-runs full ordering when the restricted normals disappear concurrently has no covering test, so this extra branch is unverified.

This test calls Ticket::call() before invoking the action, so the ticket is already excluded from the candidate snapshot; the lock-and-re-check skip path at CallNextTicket.php:119 is not actually exercised.
The test name says priority_only and normal_only calls count in fairness history, but only priority_only calls are made; no normal_only call is exercised.
The new public __invoke method lacks the PHPDoc that the project conventions require on public methods touched by a change.
The same 'is a normal ticket still waiting' query is duplicated in fairnessApplies (:80-84); extracting it into one helper would remove the repetition.
refresh() issues an extra SELECT even though the model already holds the status, called_at and called_by_user_id just saved.

review.summary: The change adds the CallNextTicket action with CallMode, NoWaitingTicketsException, ordering/fairness logic, queue-row and candidate-row locking, plus thorough Pest coverage and the required docs/CHANGELOG updates. It meets the task and contract and has no security weakness; the remaining points are minor test-coverage and PHPDoc/style nits, so it is approvable after small cleanups.
